_doc: Normalized schemas used to GENERATE denormalized multi-party tables with
mechanically-derived ground truth.
WHY THIS EXISTS. The precision corpus is hand-authored, so a perfect score
on it partly measures how well the detector matches its author's intuitions.
Here the labels are not authored at all: a wide table is produced by joining
a fact to its dimensions, and each column's party is simply THE TABLE IT
CAME FROM. The grouping is decided by the schema's original designer, and
the generator only decides how columns get renamed on the way out.
The schemas are reconstructions of well-known public data models (TPC-H,
Northwind, Sakila). They are faithful in shape -- which entities exist and
which columns belong to each -- which is the only property the labels
depend on. They are not byte-exact reproductions of the published DDL, and
nothing here needs them to be.
`fact` is the table being widened. `dimensions` are the entities it
references; each becomes one expected party. `own_columns` belong to the
fact itself and form its own party.
How a dimension's columns are renamed when denormalized. Real pipelines
differ, and the detector's affix signal is exactly what these exercise.
`initial` is expected to be UNDETECTABLE and is kept deliberately: a
one-character qualifier is below the kernel's MIN_QUALIFIER_LEN, so a
schema in TPC-H's own native style (`c_name`, `s_name`) cannot be
segmented by affix at all. Measuring that honestly is better than
choosing conventions the detector happens to win on.
